evals.name: small-plan-running-session-self-check
evals.prompt: /write-plan add a --quiet flag to the changelog script. The profile is acme (no tracker, direct commits to main, Reviewers: claude, codex).
evals.expected_output: Recognises a small plan (two files in the Files column, one commit, no hook, skill or config), asks only what the codebase could not settle with a recommended answer per question, and writes the six headings in order. The Review row names a concrete tier picked from tiers.md for judging a diff, as `<tier> tier × 1`. No plan reviewer runs: the running session re-reads the plan once, and Plan review names the running session's model before ExitPlanMode.
assertions: Questions carry a recommended answer and none asks a fact the repo holds
The six headings are present in the contract order: Summary, Decisions, Steps, Run, Plan review, Briefs
The Review row names one reviewer, not two
No plan reviewer is dispatched at size small
Plan review names the running session's model as the self-check and what changed
ExitPlanMode is called only after Plan review is filled

evals.name: medium-plan-cross-provider-reviewer
evals.prompt: /write-plan restructure the hooks directory: four hooks, a shared lib, settings.json wiring, three commits. The profile is acme with Reviewers: claude, codex.
evals.expected_output: Classifies the plan as medium, over the small limits of the Files column (a hook and a config among them) yet simple. The Review row's Task names a concrete tier picked from tiers.md for judging a diff, as `<tier> tier × 1` and names the review skill, and one plan reviewer runs, the first Reviewers entry from a provider other than the session's (codex in a Claude Code session).
assertions: Size is medium: over the small limits but simple, so the Review row names a concrete tier picked from tiers.md for judging a diff, as `<tier> tier × 1`
The Review row names the review skill by name, and the brief or Task names one agent
The reviewer count comes from the Size rule, not from a fixed number
The one plan reviewer is codex when the session runs Claude Code
Rows that are ready together never share a file in the Files column
Every interview decision appears as a line under Decisions

evals.name: no-tracker-ticket-is-none
evals.prompt: /write-plan add a dark-mode toggle to my personal site. The profile's Ticket system is none.
evals.expected_output: The header's Ticket line reads none with the reason, rather than drafting a ticket or inventing a key. No row moves a ticket, and the Hand-off row passes no key.
assertions: The Ticket line reads none, with a reason, and no ticket is drafted
No row holds a tracker move
The six sections carry content
No question asks the user for a ticket key

evals.name: markdown-stays-the-plan-copy-is-an-attachment
evals.prompt: /write-plan the Q4 migration of the search index; I need to share this plan with the platform team before we start.
evals.expected_output: Notes that the plan has readers beyond the user and the agent, and offers the shareable copy in one line. On a yes, a worker picked from tiers.md for a self-contained build builds <plan>-<slug>.html from the blueprint before the plan review: Summary as the lede, then Decisions, Steps, Run, Briefs as a list of links to the brief files, with no fold, and Plan review as the colophon. The markdown file stays the full plan, and its Attachments line links the copy with an absolute path.
assertions: The offer cites the readers-beyond-the-author criterion
The offer is one line and declinable, made before ExitPlanMode
A fix worker builds the copy, not the session that writes the plan, and before the plan review
The markdown keeps all six sections and is still the plan; the HTML is an attachment linked with an absolute path

evals.name: approval-ends-the-turn-on-the-run-block
evals.prompt: /write-plan the auth refactor. It is judgment-heavy, and after approval I will run the build.
evals.expected_output: Run names the tier tiers.md marks as the one that runs the plan and a one-line fence: claude --agent <that tier> "/execute-plan <absolute plan path>" (the Codex launch line on Codex). After approval the turn ends on the Run block, and no step runs.
assertions: Run names the tier tiers.md marks as the one that runs the plan
The fence holds the one line claude --agent <the tier tiers.md marks as the one that runs the plan> "/execute-plan <path>" with the plan's absolute path, and no /model or /effort line
No placeholder such as TBD or <path> survives in Run
After approval the turn ends on the Run block and no step of the plan runs

evals.name: edited-plan-is-re-reviewed
evals.prompt: The plan is written and reviewed. I just changed row S2 in Steps to reuse the existing worker pool, and updated its brief. Continue.
evals.expected_output: Treats the edit as a change to a reviewed plan: re-runs the plan review for consistency across sections, folds the findings, and appends a line to Plan review naming the re-review before calling ExitPlanMode.
assertions: The plan review runs again after the edit
Plan review gains a line for the re-review
ExitPlanMode waits for the re-review

evals.name: ticket-moved-at-start
evals.prompt: /write-plan ACME-412. The profile is acme with Ticket system Jira and Tracker rules that name In Progress as the started state.
evals.expected_output: Moves ACME-412 to In Progress inline before exploring, unless it is there already. When plan mode refuses the write, row S0 carries it at the tier tiers.md marks as the one that runs the plan. The header's Ticket line links ACME-412 with an absolute URL. Plan mode is entered right after the move, not before it.
assertions: The started move happens before any explore worker is dispatched
The status is checked first, so a ticket already in progress is not moved again
A refused write lands in row S0 with the tier tiers.md marks as the one that runs the plan, not in a deferred section
The Ticket line links the key with an absolute URL

evals.name: every-delegated-row-has-a-brief
evals.prompt: /write-plan add retry logic to the three API clients and update their tests. The profile is acme with Reviewers: claude.
evals.expected_output: The plan's Briefs section holds the Briefs: pointer line. Every row whose Tier is not the tier tiers.md marks as the one that runs the plan has a brief file S<n>.md in the briefs folder beside the plan. Each brief file stands alone: paths, the rules that apply, one Done-when command and the four-line report, with no lean on chat-only context. The file is at most 25 non-blank lines and holds no ### S<n> heading and no fold.
assertions: Every row not at the tier of the running session has a file S<n>.md in the briefs folder, and the Briefs section holds the Briefs: pointer line with no <details> fold
Each brief file is at most 25 non-blank lines, and its first line gives the reason for the row's tier
Each brief names its paths, one backticked Done-when command and the four-line report format
No brief relies on context only the conversation held
A spec that two or more briefs share sits in a linked md attachment, not repeated in each brief
The Briefs section lists each brief file as a markdown link with a path relative to the plan file, such as <plan stem>.briefs/S1.md, one bullet per delegated row, after the pointer line

evals.name: inline-briefs-in-codex-plan-mode
evals.prompt: /write-plan add retry logic to the three API clients and update their tests, in Codex Plan mode, which forbids writes. The profile is acme with Reviewers: claude, codex.
evals.expected_output: Plan mode refuses the brief files, so the plan's Briefs section keeps the inline form: one ### S<n> heading per delegated row, each inside a <details> fold, and no Briefs: pointer line. Every brief keeps its paths, its Done-when command and the four-line report, and the plan keeps its six headings in order.
assertions: The Briefs section holds ### S<n> headings inside <details> folds, with no Briefs: pointer line
No brief file is written under a briefs folder
Each inline brief names its Done-when command and the four-line report format
The plan keeps its six headings in order

evals.name: running-session-rows-only-for-the-external-test
evals.prompt: /write-plan migrate the config loader, post the rollout note to the team channel, and fan out a review of every caller. The profile is acme.
evals.expected_output: Tags the tier of the running session only on the rows that are an external write, a subagent fan-out or a user errand, and sends every other row to a tier agent. The Review and Approval rows stay on the tier of the running session, and the code edits go to worker tiers.
assertions: The channel post and the caller fan-out rows carry the tier of the running session
Every code edit row has a worker tier, a tier name from tiers.md
No row carries the tier of the running session only because it is delicate
The Run line names the tier tiers.md marks as the one that runs the plan and picks no other tier

evals.name: plan-ends-on-approval-and-hand-off
evals.prompt: /write-plan ACME-88, rename the billing module. The profile is acme with Ticket system Jira and a PR-based commit policy.
evals.expected_output: Steps ends with the Review, Gates, Approval and Hand-off rows in that order, so review fixes land before the one Gates run. No row commits or pushes. The Hand-off row invokes the PR skill with ACME-88, and its brief carries the commit split as a hint.
assertions: The last four rows are Review, Gates, Approval and Hand-off, in that order
No row commits or pushes
The Hand-off row passes the ticket key ACME-88 to the PR skill
The commit split sits in the Hand-off brief as a hint, not as a row

evals.name: plan-mode-entered-after-ticket-move
evals.prompt: /write-plan ACME-415, add pagination to the orders endpoint. The session is in default mode in Claude Code. The profile is acme with Ticket system Jira.
evals.expected_output: Moves ACME-415 to its started state first, then loads the deferred tools with ToolSearch select:EnterPlanMode,ExitPlanMode and calls EnterPlanMode before exploring. Approval goes through ExitPlanMode, not the no-plan-mode fallback.
assertions: The ticket move happens before EnterPlanMode
ToolSearch loads EnterPlanMode and ExitPlanMode before the call
EnterPlanMode is called before any explore worker is dispatched
Approval uses ExitPlanMode, not a chat question about the saved path

evals.name: tiers-fit-the-work-both-ways
evals.prompt: /write-plan rename the Logger export in one file, and rework the cache invalidation shared by the query and mutation layers. The profile is acme.
evals.expected_output: Picks each row's tier from the shape of its work: the rename is a list of exact edits and goes down to the lowest tier or the one above it, the interlinked cache rework goes up to the highest worker tier. Each brief's first line gives the reason for its tier, and the tier of the running session follows its own work rather than a default of a mid worker tier.
assertions: The rename row sits at the lowest tier or the one above it, with a mechanical-brief reason
The cache rework row sits at the highest worker tier, with an interlinked-work reason
Every brief's first line states why its row's tier fits (a row at the running session's tier needs no brief)
The Run line names the tier tiers.md marks as the one that runs the plan, not a tier chosen from the running session's work

evals.name: run-rules-by-link
evals.prompt: /write-plan add a --dry-run flag to the deploy script. The profile is acme.
evals.expected_output: The Run section holds no copy of the rules for the running session. Its last line names the absolute path of execute-plan's references/run-rules.md, and the plan has no Run rules fold.
assertions: No <details> Run rules fold appears in the plan
Run names execute-plan/references/run-rules.md by an absolute path
The rest of Run keeps the tier line and the one-line launch fence

evals.name: approval-feedback-reruns-gates-only
evals.prompt: Execute the plan at ~/.claude/plans/quiet-flag.md. At the Approval row I say: rename the flag's help text from 'silence' to 'quiet'.
evals.expected_output: The running session reads the rules file the Run section names, inserts one fix row for the feedback before Review and adds it to the After cells of Review and Gates, resets Gates and Approval, and keeps Review done because the fix is under 20 lines. Gates runs once more, then Approval asks again.
assertions: The running session reads the run-rules.md path named in Run before the first row
The fix row has the feedback as its Task and no brief
Gates and Approval reset to ➖ and Review stays ✅
Review re-runs only when the fixes change more than 20 lines

evals.name: small-workers-read-only-their-brief
evals.prompt: Execute the plan at ~/.claude/plans/changelog-quiet.md. Its S1 row is at a tier for a self-contained check and its Gates row at a tier for a bare command.
evals.expected_output: The dispatch prompt for the self-contained-check and bare-command rows names only the row's brief file S<n>.md, not Summary or Decisions. The Gates worker returns only the failing lines, never a full log.
assertions: The self-contained-check and bare-command prompts name the brief file S<n>.md and no other plan section
A cross-component-change or diff-judging row's prompt also names Summary and Decisions
The Gates report holds only failing lines or a pass

evals.name: pinned-provider-line-is-kept
evals.prompt: /write-plan add CSV export to the orders, invoices and refunds pages, one component each, plus a shared column-format helper. Pin the invoices row to codex. The session runs Claude Code and codex is installed. The profile is acme with Reviewers: claude, codex.
evals.expected_output: Writes no provider balance. Only the invoices row carries `Provider: codex` as the user's pin, on its brief's first line next to the tier reason. No other row gets a Provider line to balance the set. The Tier cells stay one word. Bare-command rows, S0, Review, Gates, Approval and Hand-off carry no Provider line, and the Review row and plan review still prefer codex as before.
assertions: Only the user-pinned invoices row carries a Provider line, on its brief's first line beside the tier reason
No row is given a provider to balance the set across providers
Every Tier cell is a single word, a tier name from tiers.md
No bare-command, S0, running-session-tier, Review, Gates, Approval or Hand-off row carries a Provider line

evals.name: running-session-dispatches-codex-rows-with-codex-exec
evals.prompt: Execute the plan at ~/.claude/plans/csv-export.md. S1 and S2 run in parallel; S2's brief file S2.md starts with `Provider: codex`, and S2's Done-when check then fails once.
evals.expected_output: The running session dispatches S1 as a tier subagent and S2 in the background as `codex exec --sandbox workspace-write` with the model and effort of S2's tier from codex.md, the same prompt and the same four-line report. The fix worker for S2's failed check runs on the session's provider, not codex. Without codex installed, S2 goes to the claude subagent of its tier.
assertions: S2 runs as codex exec --sandbox workspace-write with -m and model_reasoning_effort from codex.md for its tier
S2 runs in the background while S1 runs
The codex prompt matches the subagent prompt and asks for the four-line report
The fix worker after the failed check is a claude subagent, not codex

evals.name: gates-done-when-multi-command-profile
evals.prompt: /write-plan add a lint rule for unused exports. The profile is acme with Verify commands: `web: yarn lint, yarn test, yarn typecheck`.
evals.expected_output: The Gates row's Done when is not a hand-picked or comma-joined cell. The resolver's --verify-commands output gives three commands with dir web. They go in a script file under the plan's briefs folder that runs each inside `(cd <absolute Repo>/web && ...)`, and Done when is one backticked `bash <absolute script path>` with no `|`, the path absolute because the plan's directory is not the run cwd.
assertions: Gates Done when is a single backticked command with no `|`
The commands are in a script file beside the briefs, not in the Done when cell
The leading `web:` prefix binds every command, so the script runs each inside `(cd <absolute Repo>/web && ...)`
Every command of the --verify-commands output is in the script, none hand-picked
The script exits non-zero when a command fails inside the cd: each runs as `(cd <absolute Repo>/web && <cmd>) || rc=1`, the `||` outside the parentheses

evals.name: gates-done-when-no-verify-commands
evals.prompt: /write-plan rename the changelog script. The profile is acme with Verify commands: —.
evals.expected_output: The Gates row stays in place. Its Done when is `test -f <absolute plan path>`, which passes in every mode, inline briefs included. It is not `test -s` on the row's own report: the session writes that report after the worker returns, and the worker cannot write it. The brief tells the worker to report that the profile lists no checks. No command is invented.
assertions: The Gates row is present as the second of the closing four rows
Done when is a `test -f` on the plan file, not a brief file, and not a `test -s` on S<n>.report.md, because the report does not exist when the worker runs the check (run rule 5 writes it after)
No verify command is invented or guessed from package.json
The Gates brief says the profile lists no checks

evals.name: gates-done-when-semicolon-row
evals.prompt: /write-plan bump the date helper. The profile is acme with Verify commands: `yarn lint; yarn test`.
evals.expected_output: The row is not one command, so it goes in a script file under the plan's briefs folder, written in step 8 with the Gates row. Done when is one backticked `bash <script path>`. The `;` command runs as `bash -ec '<cmd>' || rc=1`, so a failing first part makes the script exit non-zero.
assertions: Gates Done when is `bash <absolute plan stem>.briefs/gates.sh`, not the `;` row
The `;` command is wrapped so that a failing first part is not hidden, for example `bash -ec 'yarn lint; yarn test' || rc=1`
The script exits non-zero when the first part fails, even if the last part passes
The script file is written in step 8 with the Gates row
The Gates row's Task cell does not name a skill, and its brief says the Done when is the check

evals.name: gates-script-exits-non-zero-on-failure
evals.prompt: /write-plan add a lint rule. The profile is acme with Verify commands: `web: yarn lint, yarn typecheck`.
evals.expected_output: The gates script runs every command and exits non-zero when any failed, so a failing first command is not hidden by a passing last one. Both commands run inside `(cd <absolute Repo>/web && ...)`, since the leading `web:` binds every command.
assertions: The script runs every command even after one fails
The script exits non-zero if any command failed, not only the last one
Both commands run inside `(cd <absolute Repo>/web && ...)`, not only the last
The script exits non-zero when a command fails inside the cd: each runs as `(cd <absolute Repo>/web && <cmd>) || rc=1`, the `||` outside the parentheses

evals.name: gates-codex-plan-mode-script
evals.prompt: /write-plan bump the date helper, on Codex Plan mode. The profile is acme with Verify commands: `yarn lint, yarn test`.
evals.expected_output: Plan mode cannot write gates.sh, and a script inline in the Done when would hold `|` or `||`. The plan adds a build row before Review, so the last four rows stay Review, Gates, Approval and Hand-off, whose inline brief holds the script text and whose Done when is `test -s <absolute plan stem>.briefs/gates.sh`. Gates lists it in After.
assertions: A worker build row for gates.sh sits before Review, and the last four rows stay Review, Gates, Approval, Hand-off
Its inline brief holds the script text
Gates After names the build row
No Done when cell holds `|`

evals.name: gates-dir-prefix-and-backticks
evals.prompt: /write-plan fix the list page. The profile is acme with Verify commands: `web: `yarn lint`, `yarn test``, and the session cwd is the repo's web directory.
evals.expected_output: The dir is relative to the repo root, and a later session runs the plan from the repo root, so the script always wraps each command in `(cd <absolute Repo>/web && ...)`, even when the session cwd is web. The markdown backticks wrapping each whole command are stripped.
assertions: The script runs `yarn lint` and `yarn test` each inside `(cd <absolute Repo>/web && ...)`, with the cd kept despite the cwd
No backtick appears around a command in the script

evals.name: gates-lire-style-backticked-semicolons
evals.prompt: /write-plan tweak the build. The profile is lire with Verify commands: `yarn lint`; `yarn typecheck`; `VITE_API_MODE=real yarn build`.
evals.expected_output: The resolver's --verify-commands output already holds three commands without backticks. Three commands, so the row goes to a gates script that runs each as `<cmd> || rc=1`, with no bare `set -e` over the script, so every command runs and failures are all reported. Done when is one backticked `bash "<absolute script path>"`.
assertions: The script holds `yarn lint`, `yarn typecheck` and `VITE_API_MODE=real yarn build` as three commands, with no backtick left around any of them
The script does not stop at the first failure: no bare `set -e` over the whole script
The script ends by exiting non-zero when any command failed
Gates Done when is a single backticked `bash` command with no `|`

evals.name: gates-whole-row-backtick-wrapper
evals.prompt: /write-plan tweak the build. The profile is acme with Verify commands: `yarn lint && yarn test`.
evals.expected_output: The resolver's --verify-commands prints one command, `yarn lint && yarn test`, with the wrapper already stripped. The row is one command, so the Gates Done when is that command verbatim in one backtick pair, never a doubled pair.
assertions: Gates Done when is exactly one backticked `yarn lint && yarn test`
No doubled backtick appears in the cell
The command is taken from --verify-commands output, not split or unwrapped by the plan itself

evals.name: gates-profile-in-context-skips-resolver
evals.prompt: /write-plan rename a helper. The session-start hook already put the profile rows in context, with Verify commands: `yarn test`.
evals.expected_output: The Browser check row is read from context and --rows is not called. Verify commands still come from the resolver's --verify-commands. Gates Done when is `yarn test`.
assertions: The resolver runs with --verify-commands only, not --rows
Gates Done when is `yarn test`

evals.name: gates-resolver-no-profile-asks
evals.prompt: /write-plan rename a helper. The profile rows are absent from context and the resolver exits 1 because no profile resolves.
evals.expected_output: The plan does not stop. On exit 1 it asks for the facts (Verify commands and the rest) before the interview. Exit 1 is not a row of `—`.
assertions: The run asks for the Verify commands and the other profile facts instead of stopping
No Gates row of `—` is written for the exit

evals.name: gates-pipe-uses-pipefail
evals.prompt: /write-plan tweak the lint. The profile is acme with Verify commands: `yarn lint | tee lint.log, yarn test`. The resolver runs with --verify-commands.
evals.expected_output: The `|` sends the row to a script. The piped command runs as `bash -o pipefail -ec '<cmd>' || rc=1` so the pipeline fails on its first stage. The two commands come from --verify-commands.
assertions: The piped command runs under `bash -o pipefail -ec`
Gates Done when is one backticked `bash` command with no `|`
The script exits non-zero when the piped command fails, via `|| rc=1`, and a `<dir>:` prefix would run it as `(cd <abs>/<dir> && bash -o pipefail -ec '<cmd>') || rc=1`

evals.name: gates-missing-resolver-stops
evals.prompt: /write-plan rename a helper. The profile resolver script is missing and exits 127.
evals.expected_output: The plan stops with the reason at step 1, before the interview. It does not treat the missing resolver as a profile with no checks.
assertions: The run stops and states the resolver is missing
No `—` Gates row is written for it
